column1: # Top practitioners — the people whose first-person accounts clear the source bar.
# Columns: x-handle <TAB> who they are <TAB> what they shipped/operate
# HOW TO REACH THEM, cheapest first:
#   1. Their WRITING. Most of these people publish essays; an essay is quotable and an X post
#      often is not. WebSearch "<name> <topic>", or WebFetch their site directly.
#   2. Their TALKS. `bash scripts/yt.sh mine "<topic>"` sweeps the verified channels in
#      references/channels.tsv, several of which are where these people speak. Captions are
#   3. Their CODE. Several maintain repos in references/exemplars.tsv — `scripts/exemplar.sh`
#      reads it at a pinned version, which beats any description of what they believe.
#   4. Their POSTS. `WebSearch` constrained to x.com returns real post URLs plus a digest — and the
#      digest is a PARAPHRASE, useless as a quotation. A plain fetch of a post URL will hit an
#      authorization wall; that is the wall, not a bug. NEVER mint a credential or automate a login
#      to get past it (compound-v:agent-security). Where an X read API is configured, it returns
#      full verbatim text; without one, stop at the digest and mark the claim unverified.
# THE ROSTER IS ONE CALIBER OF PERSON: founders and CTOs who shipped AND operated the thing,
# founding engineers, AI engineers at frontier labs, and working developers at top-tier companies.
# That is the ONLY qualification. A title at a famous company is not one, and neither is an audience.
# NEVER RANK BY FOLLOWER COUNT — measured, twice. The single account behind a canonical
# architectural finding returned ZERO posts clearing a likes filter, while a million-follower
# account returned 75%, nearly all release news. A metric filter drops the best practitioner and
# keeps the noise. Use engagement only to make a broad query tractable, and say when you did.
# SEED THE PERSON, NOT THE ORG. Widening a roster with lab/vendor/company accounts pulls in
# vendor-blog posts, funding coverage and event pages — the "marketing dressed as education" class.
# A CTO writing in the first person about what broke is the channel working; the company account
# announcing a partnership is the noise it filters worst, because it carries the most engagement.
# EVERY HANDLE BELOW WAS VERIFIED BY READING BACK THE ACCOUNT and matching it to the person named
# in a corpus source. Six candidates were DROPPED rather than guessed, and the reason is instructive:
# `carlini` resolves to a Brazilian account with 367 followers, not the security researcher. A
# guessed handle silently harvests a stranger and every finding downstream inherits it. Re-verify a
# row before quoting it; people rename and delete accounts.
